calls.head: Who drives the play: the Lightning
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Lightning have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Rangers around the middle. The ice should tilt the Lightning’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: Volume vs. Patience
calls.body: On shot volume, Tampa Bay is near the top of the league, but the Rangers are near the bottom. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the attacking zone.

surprises.head: The Rangers brought the hits
surprises.body: The Rangers are one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 211 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 119 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Lafrenière has two goals as the Rangers take down the Lightning
paras: Alexis Lafrenière got the scoring started for the Rangers just over a minute in. Lafrenière scored his second of the night midway through the first to make it 2-0, his fourth straight game with a goal. Jeffrey Viel and Matt Rempe fought later in the period. Zemgus Girgensons got the Lightning on the board late in the period, but they got no closer. Will Cuylle stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the second, and Mika Zibanejad added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-1.

The chances were closer than the score. Dylan Garand made 25 saves for the Rangers, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 19 of 22 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Marcus Pettersson had the best night of anyone.

Neither power play scored: the Rangers killed all four Lightning power plays, and the Lightning killed all four of the Rangers’. The Rangers improved to 6-2-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Bolts dropped to 4-2-0, slipping to third in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Lightning’s four-game winning streak is over.
Alexis Lafrenière has a point in five straight games, with a goal in each of the last four.
Mika Zibanejad extended his point streak against Tampa Bay to seven games.
Nikita Kucherov’s five-game point streak ended.
